transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-12 14:30 UTC, Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE); Ethan Cho (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Redwood Product); Liam O'Connor (Oceanic Head of ML); Sofia Reyes (Oceanic Product); Jonah Park (Oceanic Eng Lead)
Summary (auto): Demo of Redwood's Eval & Quality Monitoring features including prompt-set management, regression alerts, automated A/B comparisons, and integration points for API and Console. Next steps defined for pilot and security review.

00:00 Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, i'll kick off and Ethan will go deep on the eval tooling and the console demo. how's everybody doing?
00:06 Liam: Good, thanks, yeah excited to see this. We've been looking at a few tools for monitoring prompt regressions and, um, making sure rollout doesn't introduce regressions.
00:12 Ava: Perfect. Quick agenda - 1) goals and existing workflow, 2) prompt-set and evals demo in Console, 3) regression alerts + A/B comparisons, 4) next steps / POC.
00:21 Sofia: We mostly run a mix - customer support assistant and product search rewriter - both fine-tuned internally, latency requirement is sub-300ms tail for chat front-end. Cost is also a big factor.
00:30 Ethan: Got it. I'll demo three things: how to create prompt-sets, how to run automated regressions and set alerts, and how to do paired A/B evaluation. Also show how the API hooks look for automation.
00:40 Jonah: Quick Q before demo - we run in VPC for sensitive logs, can Redwood run evals without sending data to hosted index?
00:47 Ava: Yes, we have Private deployment options and you can run the control plane in your VPC or use dedicated with encrypted logs. We'll send SOC2 + security pack after the call.
00:54 Ethan: Starting Console share - (audio: screen share starts, chatter) - here is the Eval dashboard. On the left you can see Projects -> Prompt-sets -> Metrics.
01:10 Ethan: First step: create a prompt-set. You can import CSV or paste examples. Example we use in demo: 200 golden prompts for support and 150 for product search. The UI lets you attach expected outputs, categories, and tags.
01:28 Sofia: That import step - are prompt-sets versioned? We want to track changes over time.
01:34 Ethan: Yes, each import creates a version; you can diff versions and roll back. We also store checksum for each prompt so we can show drift.
01:42 Liam: Do you support programmatic prompt-set creation? We have pipelines that generate prompts from logs.
01:47 Ethan: Absolutely, there's an API endpoint /v1/evals/prompt-sets and SDK helpers. You can push programmatic sets and trigger an eval run.
01:54 Ava: (off mic) we'll include the API snippet in the follow-up.
02:10 Ethan: Demo: run a regression eval - we pick baseline model + new model variant, select prompt-set, and hit Run. Under the hood Redwood runs N comparisons per prompt and computes metrics: exact-match, BLEU-like, semantic-similarity, hallucination score, and custom heuristics you define.
02:31 Jonah: How are thresholds and alerts configured? We need to be notified on any drop > X% on key metrics for the top 10 intents.
02:42 Ethan: Alerts are rule-based - you can scope by metric, by intent tag, or by quantile (p90 latency, p50 cost). We also support anomaly detection so it can flag unexpected drifts beyond historical variance.
02:55 Sofia: Can we do A/B comparisons continuously when we rollout a new model to a fraction of traffic?
03:00 Ethan: Yes - Redwood supports canary/A-B splits, automatically capture evaluation sample from live traffic, and will report A/B deltas with significance tests. You can tie alerting to a rollout so it auto-rollback if the loss exceeds thresholds.
03:15 Liam: That rollback automation - any guardrails? We can't have noisy alerts trigger rollbacks during peak season.
03:22 Ethan: You can set time windows, minimum sample counts, and cooldowns. Also integrate with your deployment system (we have webhooks) so you control the action.
03:30 Priya: Quick note - Optimize will also surface batching/quantization suggestions per workload which can be tied to eval outcomes (i.e., if quality drops, we won't recommend aggressive quantization).
03:45 Ethan: Now switching to API view - here's the request payload for batched eval runs, sample response shows per-prompt scores. (audio: typing) transcription may say 'batched evil runs' instead of 'eval' occasionally.
04:05 Ava: (laugh) yeah, forgive the ASR - it's demo - moving on.
04:18 Ethan: Example A/B report - shows per-intent breakdown, effect size, p-value, and estimated tokens delta (cost). You can export CSV or wire this into a BI dashboard.
04:35 Jonah: For cost estimates, how accurate is the tokens delta for quantized models or different runtimes?
04:42 Ethan: We compute tokens from the request/response distribution and multiply by per-token cost of the selected model variant; for dedicated/private setups there are config values you set to reflect your unit costs. It's an estimate but we've seen within ~10-15% of actual for steady-state.
04:58 Liam: Can we run a POC where you run our prompt-sets vs our current baseline model and propose optimization suggestions?
05:05 Ava: Totally. Typical POC is 2-4 weeks: import prompts, run baseline vs candidate, iterate on thresholds, sample live traffic for A/B, and build alert rules. We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet.
05:18 Sofia: About data retention and logs - we need logs for 13 months for auditing. Is that supported?
05:25 Ava: Yes, with enterprise add-on you can get longer retention; for Private you manage retention in your environment. We'll include options in the security pack.
05:32 Ethan: Demo continues - creating a regression alert: show rule creation, scope by tag 'checkout-intent', threshold 5% drop in semantic-similarity over a 7-day rolling window. Send alerts to Slack + webhook.
05:54 Ethan: (demo noise) sometimes our transcripts say 'semantic cereal' - ASR artefact.
06:05 Jonah: How do you handle noisy labels in expected outputs? Our golden set has fuzzy answers.
06:10 Ethan: We support human-in-the-loop review flows. When an alert triggers, you can open a review board, assign samples to QA, and combine human judgement into a final metric. We persist reviewer decisions as annotations.
06:24 Liam: Any built-in evals for hallucination detection? That's our big risk for support answers.
06:29 Ethan: Yes, we have a hallucination heuristic and also allow you to plug in custom model-based classifiers. You can weight that as a primary metric for alerts.
06:38 Sofia: Can we customize the significance tests? We prefer bootstrap over asymptotic tests for small sample sizes.
06:44 Ethan: You can choose the statistical test in report settings - t-test, bootstrap, bayesian A/B are supported.
06:52 Ava: Let's go briefly through the API snippet and POC plan. (shares chat) The POC will include: 1) Redwood runs baseline eval with provided prompt-sets, 2) setup live A/B to capture 10% traffic for 2 weeks, 3) produce report & Optimize recommendations.
07:10 Jonah: Integration effort - our infra is on GCP, we use internal auth and SSO. How does auth to Redwood work for Private?
07:18 Ava: For Private we integrate with your IdP via SAML/SSO and you manage keys. For dedicated we support mTLS and team-level RBAC.
07:25 Liam: Pricing - rough idea for 2-week POC?
07:28 Ava: For a POC we typically offer a trial credit but will propose a scoped pilot price depending on token volume and dedicated hours. We'll include dedicated pilot options in the follow-up.
07:35 (silence, typing)
07:45 Ethan: Quick demo of a regression alert firing - here's a historical run where a new model dropped semantic-similarity on 'returns' intent by 7%, alert triggered, we opened a review board and rolled back.
08:02 Sofia: Love the review board - we can route to PMs and QA.
08:09 Liam: Exportability - can we push evaluation results to our data lake?
08:12 Ethan: Yes, we have S3/GCS sinks and webhooks for streaming eval rows.
08:19 Ava: Ok, let's recap next steps - we'll send SOC2/security docs, the POC plan and pricing, and Ethan will draft the benchmark plan. Liam to provide prompt-sets and a week of logs.
08:32 Liam: sounds good. One more minor ask - can Redwood's Optimize flag suggestions include latency impact per suggestion?
08:38 Priya: Yes we can surface estimated latency and cost tradeoffs per suggestion, and link to model variant and quantization profile.
08:46 Ava: Great. Anything else from Oceanic?
08:49 Sofia: No, that covers it. thanks.
08:52 Ava: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
09:00 End of recording.
